stem: Where is a lateral external angular dermoid cyst most commonly located in a toddler?

options.text: Over the lateral border of the eyebrow.
Inside the mouth on the floor of the mandible.

explanation: This specific location corresponds to the embryological junction of the frontonasal and maxillary processes.
rationale: This cyst occurs at a specific junction of facial processes near the eye.

optionExplanations.A: The submental region is a site for midline dermoids, not lateral external angular ones.
optionExplanations.B: This specific location corresponds to the embryological junction of the frontonasal and maxillary processes.
optionExplanations.C: Masses deep to the sternomastoid are usually branchial remnants or lymph nodes, not angular dermoid cysts.
optionExplanations.D: A lesion in this area would more likely be a ranula or a plunging ranula.

source.hint: This cyst occurs at a specific junction of facial processes near the eye.
